rule: confluence:6497338582 outranks repo:addressbook on data format, but by its own claim p1-103 it defines no telephone rule, allowed characters or error message, so the only enforceable part of its 'string (telephone, max 20)' is the 20-character limit and its example +44 1733 560890, both of which today's free text already meets; the wording of any error is the prototype's under ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 64, and the prototype shows no phone format error (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-133), while ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claims 10 and 13 keep the address book's real validation (ruling cv-044) and allow no question where the sources leave nothing to choose.
outcome: Phone stays free text of up to 20 characters in the INS frontend's address form and the address book API, with the hint 'For international numbers include the country code' and the existing 'Telephone number must be 20 characters or less' message; no telephone-format check and no new error message are added. The germinal data fields outrank the address book, but they name a 'telephone' type without defining it (no rule, allowed characters or message), so the 20-character limit and acceptance of international numbers such as +44 1733 560890 are all they require, and today's free text meets both; the prototype, which owns error wording, shows no phone format error, and the address book's ruling cv-044 is the real validation that stands.
